chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'How much is the reprimand (Ta'zir)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Less than the Penalty (Hadd).' I said, 'Less than eighty?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but it is less than forty, for it is the Penalty (Hadd) of the slave.' I said, 'And how much is that?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'According to what the Governor sees fit regarding the sin of the man and the strength of his body.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Ta'zir and Hadd in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the jurisprudential boundary of Ta'zir, distinguishing it from fixed Hadd penalties by anchoring it within the range of 40 to 80 lashes. It highlights the principle of judicial discretion (Ijtihad al-Wali), where the specific punishment is calibrated not just by the crime's severity but also by the offender's physical capacity, reflecting the Shia emphasis on equity and adaptability in legal application.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al hassan Bin Ali, from Hammad Bin Usman who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘How much is the reprimand?’ So heasws said: ‘Less than the Penalty (Hadd)’. I said, ‘Less than eighty (lashes)?’ So heasws said: ‘No, but it is less than the forty (lashes), for it is a Penalty (Hadd) of the owned (slaves)’. I said, ‘And how much is that?’ Heasws said: ‘Upon the measurement of what the guardian sees fit from a sin of the man, and strength of his body’.
